title: Retroactive Conformance via Extension

docs.title: Extensions — Adding Protocol Conformance with an Extension

hints: You can add a protocol conformance to an existing type in an extension.
Conform `Int` and `String`, then conform `Array` only `where Element: Summarizable`.
`extension Array: Summarizable where Element: Summarizable { var summary: String { "[" + map(\.summary).joined(separator: ",") + "]" } }`.
jsBridge: **Retroactive conformance**: you can make `Int` or `Array` adopt your protocol after the fact. TS gets this for free structurally, while nominal Swift needs an explicit `extension Int: Summarizable`. Conditional conformance (`where Element: Summarizable`) is what makes it powerful.

compass.q: In TS, `Int` would "conform" automatically if it had `summary`. What does Swift's explicit conformance buy you?
What's the Swift 6 warning about retroactively conforming a type you don't own to a protocol you don't own (`@retroactive`)?
